title: A recurring whole marks prohibition rather than descriptive action
summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks negative deontic prohibition of an otherwise stable action, rather than descriptive action or a broader obligation/condition.

design.mechanism: A candidate scopes a negative deontic prohibition over a following action field; this proposal does not claim non-applicability, requirement, or conditionality.
design.unit: Complete candidate occurrences with independently coded following action, prohibition-versus-neutral status, and matched descriptive action contexts; requirement and non-applicability are excluded from the target.
design.contrast: Candidate-bearing forbidden action versus candidate-free descriptive action and candidate-bearing permitted action under the same action/material frame; requirement and conditional contexts are held out.
design.prediction: The candidate should predict a reproducible prohibition status while leaving action identity stable. A descriptive-action model predicts no prohibition interaction, while a requirement model predicts positive obligation rather than the predeclared negative status.
design.falsifier: If independently bound matched contexts show no prohibition-status interaction, or if the candidate tracks action/material identity without negative deontic status, this narrow prohibition hypothesis fails. A requirement or non-applicability result is a rival outcome, not evidence for this target.
design.availability: Independent permission/prohibition and action-status endpoint availability_unknown; no source report supplies a Voynich deontic binding.
design.related: IDEA000028 already contains forbidden action in its broader modal-obligation design. Retain this only as a narrower prohibition specialization with a distinct negative-status falsifier; it is not a novel general modality claim. It is also related to IDEA000030/31/34, whose causal, contrast, and exception targets remain distinct.
design.countermodel: A register/template wrapper can correlate with imperative-looking fields and apparent negative status while encoding neither prohibition nor modality; action and register imbalance can mimic the interaction.
